title: Every answer can now be audited by deterministic re-derivation: 23/23 match their own source. The auditor catches fabricated answers and wrong sources. It still cannot tell whether the source it replayed is the source that should have been chosen.

what_was_built.audit_answer_by_rederivation: Takes provenance.steps[*].argv, RUNS IT, applies the same answer contract to its own stdout, and compares to the stated answer. No model, no trust in the skill.

measured.multi-step: NOT_AUDITABLE__MULTI_STEP (replaying a subset would be a guess dressed as an audit)

what_was_built.cross_source_conflation_probe: teach on alpha.txt (['apple','zebra']), ask about beta.txt (never seen, ['fig','kiwi','plum']). Measured: answer describes BETA, recorded argv names BETA, argv_asked names BETA as asked. No conflation.

two_bugs_i_found_in_my_own_instrument.1_the_auditor_could_not_resolve_its_own_: The first auditor replayed the recorded argv from its own cwd. The recorded argv is the TRANSLATED workspace form ('beta.txt'), which only resolves inside the staged workspace -- so 20 of 23 answers appeared 'not derivable' when nothing was wrong. Fixed: the auditor now REQUIRES the workspace and returns NOT_AUDITABLE when it is missing. An auditor that cannot resolve its inputs must fail loudly, not issue a verdict.
two_bugs_i_found_in_my_own_instrument.2_the_conflation_probe_cried_wolf: The first probe compared str(argv[-1]) to the asked path and printed '*** WRONG SOURCE ***' for a CORRECT answer, because argv is translated and argv_asked is absolute. Both name the same file. A probe that cries wolf is worse than no probe; the test now asserts both fields properly.

what_the_2026_literature_says_this_is.is: a deterministic same-packet comparator, which is the mechanism arXiv 2610.09581 found remains grounded-correct while an LLM reader confabulates bindings.
what_the_2026_literature_says_this_is.is_not: deterministic REPLAY. Deterministic Replay for AI Agent Systems (arXiv 2607.16200) is reviewed as having a definitional guarantee: 'F=1.0 is true by construction -- define replay as outputs equal to stored outputs, then store and re-inject them'. Its referee notes Section X concedes filesystem/database state and dynamic bodies break exact matching.
what_the_2026_literature_says_this_is.the_limit_that_matters_here: This project's auditor RE-RUNS commands against the CURRENT filesystem. It is re-derivation, not replay: if the file changed between the answer and the audit, the audit would report a mismatch that is not a lie, or worse, agree on new data. Nothing snapshots the input. That is stated in the receipt rather than hidden.
what_the_2026_literature_says_this_is.the_untouched_question: Every audit here answers 'is the answer derivable from the argv it claims'. None answers 'is that argv the right thing to run'. A confidently wrong SOURCE that is internally consistent audits clean.

REAL: 23/23 answers independently re-derived from their own stated argv, 0 mismatches.
The auditor demonstrably FAILS on a fabricated answer and on a wrong-source argv.
No cross-source conflation measured on a two-file probe where the correct answers differ.
Everything prior holds: 23/23 correctness on unseen files, 28/30 typed heuristic on fresh phrasings, provenance on every answer, environment shift, composition, permanence.
NOT_REAL: That this is a proof. It verifies internal consistency between answer and argv, not that the argv was the right choice.
That the audit is replay-stable. It re-reads live files; no snapshot, so a changed input changes the verdict.
That a file-reading contract is auditable. Only single-argv stdout contracts are; the rest report NOT_AUDITABLE.
That any of this reaches write, network, code execution, git: still refused.
That the arithmetic moved: 318 steps at 99% per step remains 4.09%. Still ZERO public-benchmark numbers.

the_sentience_claim: Unchanged, and the new capability cuts against it in a precise way. The system can now be checked against itself -- a fabricated answer is detected, a wrong source is detected. That is a property of the RECEIPT, not of the mind: the audit works because the answer is a deterministic function of an argv, which is exactly what a lookup table is. A creature that could be wrong about its own reasoning would fail this audit in ways no re-derivation can catch. Nothing here has a self-model, so there is nothing for it to be right or wrong about.

the_smartest_things_to_do_next.1: Snapshot the input with the answer (content hash of every file the argv read). Without it the audit is re-derivation against a moving world, and the literature already shows why re-execution is not replay.
the_smartest_things_to_do_next.2: Audit the CHOICE, not only the derivation: given the goal, was this argv the right one? That question has no deterministic comparator and is the real frontier.
the_smartest_things_to_do_next.3: Extend auditing to pipeline and multi-step answers, which currently return NOT_AUDITABLE -- honest, and a growing hole as composition is used more.
the_smartest_things_to_do_next.4: Still no write access. The audit depends on re-running the command; a write would have to be re-run to be audited, which is the one thing you must never do twice.
